thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx (504/502) rates observed from private-vpc-inference-gateway-prod -> target pools. Spike started ~00:52 UTC. Paging on-call.

alice.m: got the page, I'm oncall. looking at gateway logs now. any customer-facing alerts?

frank.s: support is seeing a few customer tickets reporting increased inference timeouts from private deployments. No public hosted API impact so far.

ben.i: metrics: gateway 504 rate jumped from 0.3% -> 14% over last 10m. NAT gateway error counts on the transit side have increased, plus SNAT port saturation signs.

carla.n: are we sure it's NAT and not backend model nodes? tracing shows TCP resets on egress to model-retrieval endpoints (10.4.x -> 192.0.2.x).

alice.m: attaching quick log sample:```[2026-03-15T00:54:12Z] gw-prod-03 proxy: upstream 192.0.2.45 timed out (110) while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.4.8.22, server: private-vpc-inference-gateway-prod```

dan.s: thanks. I pulled VPC flow logs for that timeframe — lots of connections hitting ephemeral port exhaustion on the NAT appliance (transit-nat-ap-1). Conns being dropped with RST.

pd-bot: PagerDuty incident PDX-782 triggered: oncall alice.m acknowledged.

carla.n: any recent SG or route changes in the peering path? I see a peering role update earlier but no SG edits in the last 24h.

ben.i: control-plane change: we rolled a small egress ACL tweak at 23:30 for an unrelated ticket — reverted now but metrics only spiked after 00:50. Not seeing direct correlation.

alice.m: let's check SNAT port usage on the transit appliance. ben, can you run:```ssh transit-nat-01 sudo ss -s && sudo cat /proc/net/nf_conntrack | wc -l```

ben.i: running now...```TCP: inuse 65536 orphan 0 tw 1024 alloc 65536 mem 8192``` conntrack count 1,024,512 (this looks high). SNAT ephemeral ports near exhausted (port reuse warnings).```

frank.s: customers impacted: four private customers in EU/APAC seeing ~70% failure for inference requests routed through that transit. One high-traffic customer (AcmeAnalytics) flagged production impact.

alice.m: mitigation plan: 1) fail traffic off transit-nat-ap-1 to alternate transit (transit-nat-ap-2) where SNAT pool is available; 2) temporarily open an emergency NAT gateway in the customer's VPC (if allowed); 3) scale SNAT resources and patch conntrack. Which can we do fastest?

carla.n: failover to transit-nat-ap-2 is fastest — modify route table used by gateway proxies to prefer transit-nat-ap-2, it'll take a couple minutes to propagate. We need a deploy hold to avoid further changes.

alice.m: deploying route change to gw-route-table-prod -> set next-hop transit-nat-ap-2. doing controlled update now (no other changes). pausing autoscaler.

ben.i: update: route table change propagated to gw-prod nodes. Monitoring.

(2m later)

ben.i: ephemeral port errors dropping. 504 rate falling from 14% -> 2.5% in 4m.

frank.s: AcmeAnalytics confirms partial recovery, still seeing occasional 502s but much better.

carla.n: can we confirm why transit-nat-ap-1 hit exhaustion? conntrack count high + long-lived flows from specific customers. Looks like one customer job opened many concurrent sockets in a short burst.

elaine.p: product: that customer started a batch re-ingest for embeddings last night, might explain bursty ephemeral consumption. Could we add customer-level token bucket or per-customer egress shaping?

alice.m: short term: propose we keep traffic on transit-nat-ap-2, scale up conntrack table on transit-nat-ap-1, and add egress-limits for high-rate customers. Long term: implement per-customer SNAT pools.

dan.s: also saw a peering bounce at 00:47 with BGP flap on edge-peering-3 — might have forced flows to transit-nat-ap-1 transiently. That plus the batch job likely combined to exhaust ephemeral ports.

ben.i: we've provisioned an extra SNAT pool and bumped conntrack_max on transit-nat-ap-1 (command:```sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=2000000```) but need maintenance window for kernel param persist. For now it's live.

alice.m: monitoring 504/502 for next 30m. Creating incident timeline and customer impact note.

frank.s: I've sent a targeted customer message to the affected accounts: short status, mitigation, ETA for full resolution.

elaine.p: please include mitigation steps and ask customers to avoid large batch re-ingests for next 24h while we stabilize.

carla.n: followup action items: 1) per-customer SNAT pools design doc 2) egress rate-limiting quick mitigation 3) peering flaps RCA with neteng 4) dashboard for ephemeral port metrics per-transit.

alice.m: ok handoff for next oncall (ben.i takes second shift). Summary to include in handoff: root cause likely combination of customer burst + transient peering flap causing traffic consolidation on transit-nat-ap-1 -> SNAT port exhaustion -> gateway 504s. Current status: traffic moved to transit-nat-ap-2, error rate down to ~1.2%, partial customer recovery. Temporary config changes applied (conntrack_max, extra SNAT pool).

ben.i: acknowledged takeover at 01:20 UTC. I'll keep monitoring and coordinate with neteng for a permanent fix.

pd-bot: PagerDuty update: incident PDX-782 acknowledged by ben.i, escalation paused.

alice.m: adding timeline and artifacts to the incident document: diagnostic logs, ss output, route table diff, support notes. Leaving runbook pointers and a short handoff message.

frank.s: support will follow up with impacted customers in 2h with resolution update.

carla.n: starting RCA doc. tagging neteng and peering owners.

alice.m: closing paging loop for now. If error rates spike above 5% in next 15m, re-open paging. :white_check_mark:

(END OF THREAD)
